title: Reduced fixed locus of a contracting deformation
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_kX$ be a geometric correspondence with fixed scheme $F$ and projections $i_F:F\to C$, $d:F\to X$ as in [def-trf-fixed-scheme]. Let $y_C\in C(k)$ and $y_X\in X(k)$ be reduced closed points, and put $Z=\{y_X\}$. Assume $F=\{y_C\}$ as a reduced subscheme of $C$, $c_1^{-1}(Z)=\{y_C\}$ scheme-theoretically, and $c_2(y_C)=y_X$. Write $I_Z$ for the ideal sheaf of $Z$ and $J=c_1^{\cdot}I_Z\mathcal O_C$ for the ideal of $y_C$. Assume
$$c_2^{\cdot}I_Z\mathcal O_C\subseteq J,\qquad (c_2^{\cdot}I_Z)^n\mathcal O_C\subseteq J^{n+1}\quad\text{for some }n\geq1.$$
Use the Rees deformation over $D=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t]_{(t)})$ of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry], with special-fibre legs $b_i:N_{c^{-1}(Z\times Z)/C}\to N_{Z/X}$. Then $c^{-1}(Z\times Z)=\{y_C\}$ scheme-theoretically, the image of $b_2$ is set-theoretically supported on the zero section $Z$, and $b_1^{-1}(Z)=\{y_C\}$ scheme-theoretically. The special fibre of $\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)$ is set-theoretically supported on $y_C$. The canonical closed immersion
$$\widetilde F_{d^{-1}Z}= (y_C)_D\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fix}(\widetilde c)$$
is an isomorphism on generic fibres and induces an isomorphism on reductions. Thus the lifted fixed scheme is a nilpotent thickening of the constant point deformation.
